result:
The regimen is in: title soaks switch to MAX performance and fan before the app starts and return to REST on every exit. It's proven on the Nova's hardware. PR #444 stays in draft, waiting on CI and on the Thor.

**Values** (the enums from the OEM settings code; the choices were then checked on the Nova):

| | performance_mode | fan_mode |
|---|---|---|
| MAX | 2 (HIGH) | 5 (SPORT) |
| REST | 0 (NORMAL) | 4 (SMART) |

I posted the REST values on the PR for `host-tools/device_rest.conf`.

**Proof on the Nova (idle, no title):**
- `performance_mode` 0/1/2 sets the GPU minimum clock to 401/550/615 MHz, and the big-core clock follows.
- `fan_mode` 0 stops the fan, 1–4 all hold the same duty (12000), and 5 doubles it (25000, 8100 rpm).
- I first picked fan mode 3 as MAX. The registered prediction said that leg would fail if 3 wasn't the maximum, and it failed, so MAX is now 5.

**Nova pilot** (REST, MAX, REST on Crimson Skies hands-off): all legs pass except the labelled +5% fps guess.
- The MAX arm really ran at MAX: GPU minimum 615 vs 401 MHz, fan 25000 vs about 14000.
- REST came back every time, including after a TERM on the device (exit code 143, REST read back as 0/4).
- fps was 29 in every arm, because Crimson's hands-off stretch is capped near 30 fps, so this title can't show a clock effect.
- Two deviations from the registration, both in NOTES:
  - The judge reads the `gfps=` value rather than the registered line-cadence reader, because on this build that line is printed every ~2 s.
  - The third arm was cut at 200 s to keep the hold under 30 minutes.

**My mistake, fixed:** in the first two Nova sessions my hand-run arms were killed after 33–103 s. My session script used a scratch lease file instead of the Nova's real lease. Other Claude sessions' Stop hooks force-stop hakuX on any device whose lease is stale, and they don't read `dispatch/hold/`. With the real lease, the third session ran clean. I told the host on the PR that a hold alone doesn't protect a device from those hooks.

**Code:**
- `soak_title.sh` switches to MAX before `am start`. REST is restored only from the exit trap. TERM and INT now exit through it; before, a TERM went back into the hold loop.
- pgraph/disc runs are untouched.
- The fields land in `perf_regimen.json` in each result dir, but not yet in result.json. That needs a ~12-line patch to `dispatcher.sh`, which PR #440 claims; the board request with the patch is filed.
- The new selftest (`84-perf-regimen.sh`) is 17/17, with a mutant that must fail for each exit path. The existing soak selftest (89) is 45/45 and preflight passes, both after merging master.

**Still waiting:**
- **CI** on head 55823b54cf.
- **The Thor**, for its write proof and the Blinx pilot (registered, not run). It was at 43% battery, below the 50% start floor, and is held by lane.titlestate until 16:41 PDT.

The `waiting:` comment is on the PR, and NOTES §5b says what to do on resume. If the Thor still doesn't qualify then, I'll mark the PR ready and leave the Thor pilot as a named follow-up.
